calls_log.text: NBC News projects Democratic holds in Delaware, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Rhode Island (exact call times not shown on NBC's page; first seen by this tracker at 6:40 PM MT). No net change.

NBC News projects Roy Cooper (D) wins North Carolina's open Senate seat (Tillis retiring), the first Senate seat to change party tonight. Cooper leads 66.8% to 31.6% at 56.2% in per AP, with Republican-leaning Election Day votes still to come.

Decision Desk HQ projects Ashley Moody (R) wins Florida's Senate special. A Republican hold, so no net change; Moody leads 49.7% to 49.2% at 83.8% in per AP, far closer than the Moody +5.8 polling average.
Decision Desk HQ projects Chris Pappas (D) wins New Hampshire's open Senate seat. A Democratic hold, so no net change.

calls_log.text: AP now also calls Georgia for Jon Ossoff (D).

calls_log.by: Decision Desk HQ; NBC News followed at 5:31 PM MT
calls_log.text: Decision Desk HQ and NBC News project Jon Ossoff (D) wins re-election in Georgia. A Democratic hold, so no net change; Democrats still need a net gain of 4 seats for control.
Decision Desk HQ projects Mark Warner (D) wins Virginia's Senate race. A Democratic hold, so no net change toward control.

alerts.text: NBC News projects five safe Democratic holds (DE, IL, MA, NJ, RI) and a Republican hold in West Virginia. Senate: Democrats 43 (34 not up + 9 won), Republicans 33 (31 not up + 2 won), 24 of 35 not yet called; Democrats still need a net +3 more. AP House calls via NBC: D 49, R 20.
NBC News projects Cooper (D) wins North Carolina, a flip from R; Democrats now need a net +3 for Senate control. House calls per AP via NBC: D 41, R 17.

North Carolina: first big count, 53.3% in per AP; Cooper (D) 67.7%, Whatley (R) 30.7%, mostly early votes that lean Democratic, so a large red shift is expected as Election Day ballots report. South Carolina: Andrews (D) 52.0%, Graham (R) 46.4% at 30.7% in.

Decision Desk HQ calls Florida's Senate special for Moody (R) and New Hampshire for Pappas (D), both holds. Senate calls so far: D 3 holds, R 1 hold, no seats changed party. AP added its Georgia call for Ossoff at 5:59 PM MT.
Florida special, 83.7% in: Moody (R) 49.6%, Nixon (D) 49.2%, lead flipped from Nixon. South Carolina, 15.5% in: Andrews (D) 51.5%, Graham (R) 47.2%.
South Carolina Senate, 9.3% in: Andrews (D) 51.2%, Graham (R) 47.6%, lead flipped from Graham; mostly early vote. Florida special, 81.6% in: Nixon (D) 49.6%, Moody (R) 49.3%.

Florida Senate special, 74.2% in: Nixon (D) 50.1%, Moody (R) 48.8%, Nixon's lead narrows to 1.3 points from 2.7 as Election Day votes come in. Ohio special, 6.2% in: Brown (D) 66.8%, Husted (R) 30.3%, early and absentee ballots counted first.

Florida Senate special, 70.5% in: Nixon (D) 50.8%, Moody (R) 48.1%, a 2.7-point Nixon lead, up from 0.9 at 63.7% in. Remaining vote is mostly Election Day and panhandle ballots, which have leaned Republican.
Georgia Senate called for Jon Ossoff (D) by Decision Desk HQ (5:18 PM MT) and NBC News (5:31 PM MT). Democratic hold; no net change toward control.

Florida Senate special, 63.7% in: Nixon (D) 49.9%, Moody (R) 49.0%, a 0.9-point Nixon lead, down from 1.4 at 54% in. Remaining vote is mostly Election Day and panhandle ballots, which have leaned Republican.

Polls closed at 5:30 PM MT in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia. No votes counted yet in NC or OH Senate. Both report early and mail ballots first, which tend to lean Democratic before Election Day votes come in.

Florida Senate special, 54% in: Nixon (D) 50.2%, Moody (R) 48.8%, a 1.4-point Nixon lead, down from 4.0 at about 50% in. Georgia, 22% in: Ossoff (D) 68.7%, Collins (R) 31.3%, mostly early and mail ballots so far.

Florida Senate special, est. 36% in: Nixon (D) 1,606,824 (52.3%), Moody (R) 1,436,546 (46.7%), a 5.6-point Nixon lead, down from 8.6 at 25% in. Election Day votes are now being added and have leaned Republican.
Florida Senate special, est. 25% in: Nixon (D) 53.8%, Moody (R) 45.2% (DDHQ). Mostly early/mail ballots; expect a shift toward Moody as Election Day votes are counted.

Polls closed at 5:00 PM MT in GA, SC, most of FL and most of NH. No votes reported and no calls yet. Watch for a shift: GA and FL report early/mail ballots first, which tend to make Democrats look stronger early before Election Day votes come in.

map_notes: States not listed in races are shown grey (no tracked Senate race on this site).
takeaways_summary: Democrats have flipped North Carolina (NBC News projection), the only Senate seat to change party so far, so they need a net gain of 3 more for control; every other call has been an expected hold. Florida, the only key race nearly fully counted, finished far closer than expected (Moody R+2.7 at 96% in vs a Moody +5.8 polling average and Trump +13.1 in 2024), pointing left of both 2022 and 2024. Early counts in South Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas and Michigan lean Democratic but are mostly early and mail ballots, and Republican-leaning Election Day votes are still out.

takeaways.headline: Expected holds called: five for Democrats, one for Republicans
takeaways.detail: NBC News projects Democrats hold Delaware, Illinois, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Rhode Island, and Republicans hold West Virginia. None change party, so Democrats still need a net gain of 3 more seats for a 51-seat majority. In the competitive races, South Carolina's Andrews (D) leads by 6.9 points (D+6.9) at 49% in, versus a Graham +2.2 polling average, but Republican-leaning Election Day votes are still being counted.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: 6:30 digest: one Democratic flip, Florida far closer than polls
takeaways.detail: Senate calls so far: Democrats held Virginia, Georgia and New Hampshire and flipped North Carolina; Republicans held Florida's special (DDHQ, NBC, AP). Democrats need a net +3 more for 51. Florida is the only key race nearly complete: Moody R+2.1 at 94% in vs a Moody +5.8 polling average, a 3.7-point miss toward Democrats so far. One state isn't enough to call polling error correlated; North Carolina (D+35.2 at 56.2% in) and South Carolina (D+5.3 at 38.6% in vs Graham +2.2) are still mostly early votes. AP House calls via NBC: D 41, R 17.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: Democrats flip North Carolina's Senate seat, NBC News projects
takeaways.detail: NBC News projects Roy Cooper (D) beats Michael Whatley (R) for the seat Thom Tillis (R) is leaving, the first Senate seat to change party tonight. Cooper leads 66.8% to 31.6% at 56.2% in per AP; the final polling average was Cooper +11.2 and Trump won North Carolina by 3.2 points in 2024. Democrats now need a net gain of 3 more seats to reach 51.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: North Carolina's first big count: Cooper (D) far ahead on early votes
takeaways.detail: With 53.3% of the expected vote in per AP, Roy Cooper (D) leads Michael Whatley (R) 67.7% to 30.7%, a 37-point Democratic lead (D+37.0). North Carolina reports early and mail ballots first, which lean Democratic, so expect the margin to shrink a lot as Election Day votes come in; the final polling average was Cooper +11.2 and Trump won the state by 3.2 points in 2024. South Carolina's Andrews (D) lead widened to 52.0% to 46.4% (D+5.6) at 30.7% in, versus a Graham +2.2 polling average. NBC's Decision Desk now rates Ohio as leaning Democratic, which is not a call.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: Florida called for Moody (R), but much closer than polls; no Senate seat has flipped
takeaways.detail: Decision Desk HQ projected Ashley Moody (R) the winner of Florida's special at 6:00 PM MT. AP data via NBC News shows Moody up 49.7% to 49.2% (R+0.5) at 83.8% in, versus a Moody +5.8 final polling average and Trump's 13.1-point 2024 win, so Democrats are running about 5 points better than polls there with Republican-leaning ballots still out. Decision Desk HQ also called New Hampshire for Chris Pappas (D). All four Senate calls are holds, so Democrats still need a net gain of 4. Worse than expected for Republicans in Florida's margin, as expected in the seat count.
takeaways.source_label: Decision Desk HQ; AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: Florida lead flips to Moody (R) as Election Day votes come in
takeaways.detail: Per AP data via NBC News, Ashley Moody (R) now leads Angie Nixon (D) 49.6% to 49.2% (R+0.4, meaning Moody ahead by 0.4 points) with 83.7% in, after Nixon led by 0.3 at 81.6% in. That is still well short of the Moody +5.8 final polling average and Trump's 13.1-point 2024 win, but the remaining Election Day and panhandle votes have historically leaned Republican. Not called.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: South Carolina early lead flips to Andrews; Florida now nearly tied
takeaways.detail: Per AP data via NBC News, Annie Andrews (D) leads Darline Graham (R) 51.2% to 47.6% (D+3.6, meaning Andrews ahead by 3.6 points) with 9.3% in, after Graham led at 3.1% in. The final polling average was Graham +2.2 and Trump won South Carolina by 17.9 in 2024, but this is mostly early vote, which leans Democratic; Election Day votes still to come have leaned Republican. In Florida, Nixon (D) leads Moody (R) 49.6% to 49.3% at 81.6% in, down from D+1.3.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: Florida tightens: Nixon's lead shrinks to 1.3 points with 74% in
takeaways.detail: Per AP data via NBC News, Angie Nixon (D) leads Ashley Moody (R) 50.1% to 48.8% (D+1.3, meaning Nixon ahead by 1.3 points), down from D+2.7 at 70.5% in, as Republican-leaning Election Day ballots are added. That is still well ahead of the Moody +5.8 final polling average. In Ohio, Brown (D) leads Husted (R) 66.8% to 30.3% at 6.2% in, but those are mostly early and absentee ballots that Ohio reports first and that lean Democratic.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: Nixon's Florida lead widens to 2.7 points with 70% in
takeaways.detail: Per AP data via NBC News, Angie Nixon (D) leads Ashley Moody (R) 50.8% to 48.1% (D+2.7, meaning Nixon ahead by 2.7 points) with 70.5% of the expected vote in, up from D+0.9 at 63.7%. The final polling average was Moody +5.8 and Trump won Florida by 13.1 points in 2024. Decision Desk HQ's own count at about 68% in shows Nixon +3.3. Ohio's first returns (1% in) show Husted (R) +4.1, too early to read.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News; Decision Desk HQ

takeaways.headline: Ossoff projected to win Georgia; Florida narrows to under 1 point
takeaways.detail: Decision Desk HQ (5:18 PM MT) and NBC News (5:31 PM MT) project Jon Ossoff (D) keeps his Georgia seat, a Democratic hold that does not change the math for control. In Florida, with 63.7% in per AP data, Angie Nixon (D) leads Ashley Moody (R) 49.9% to 49.0% (D+0.9, meaning Nixon ahead by 0.9 points), down from 1.4 points; the final polling average was Moody +5.8. Polls also closed in North Carolina and Ohio at 5:30 PM MT.
takeaways.source_label: Decision Desk HQ; AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: Florida Senate race tightens to 1.4 points; Georgia's early count favors Ossoff
takeaways.detail: With 54% in per AP data, Angie Nixon (D) leads Ashley Moody (R) 50.2% to 48.8%, a 1.4-point lead (D+1.4), down from 4.0 points about 10 minutes earlier as Election Day votes are added. The final polling average was Moody +5.8. In Georgia, Jon Ossoff (D) leads Mike Collins (R) 68.7% to 31.3% with 22% in, but that count is mostly early and mail ballots that lean Democratic; expect it to narrow.
takeaways.source_label: AP via NBC News

takeaways.headline: First Senate call: Warner holds Virginia; Florida's early count favors Nixon
takeaways.detail: Decision Desk HQ projected Mark Warner (D) the winner in Virginia at 5:00 PM MT, a Democratic hold. In Florida's Senate special, DDHQ had Angie Nixon (D) at 53.8% to Ashley Moody (R) at 45.2% with an estimated 25% in at 5:09 PM MT. The final polling average was Moody +5.8. Expect that lead to shrink as Election Day votes are added; Florida reports early and mail ballots first.
takeaways.source_label: Decision Desk HQ

takeaways.headline: First key polls closed: Georgia, South Carolina, most of Florida and New Hampshire
takeaways.detail: No votes had been reported in these Senate races as of 5:02 PM MT and nothing has been called. In Georgia and Florida the first numbers are usually early and mail ballots, which have leaned Democratic, so early leads may overstate Democrats until Election Day votes are counted. Final polling averages: Georgia D+9.4 (Democrat ahead by 9.4 points), New Hampshire D+8.6, South Carolina R+2.2, Florida R+5.8.
takeaways.source_label: NPR/AP results page; tracker polling averages (RCP, Electoral-Vote, US Polling Data)

takeaways.headline: Pre-closing read: early vote still mixed, tilting slightly left vs 2022
takeaways.detail: New counts: Kansas early ballots reached 505,641 with registered Republicans ahead by 3.6 points (up from 2.4 a day earlier). Maine reached 307,719, a 23.7-point Democratic registration edge versus 25.2 at the same point in 2022. Final polling averages moved slightly toward Democrats in AK, IA, KS, ME, OH and NC and slightly toward Republicans in TX. Registration isn't vote choice, and Republicans tend to vote more on Election Day.
takeaways.source_label: Call the Map (state and county offices); Electoral-Vote.com averages

takeaways.headline: Ohio's early vote reached 1.75 million ballots
takeaways.detail: Ohio counted 1,754,731 early ballots through Monday (653,742 by mail, 1,100,989 in person), up 24,619 from the prior count. Ohio doesn't report party for early voters, so this is turnout, not direction. The overall read vs 2022 is still mixed with a slight tilt left, at low confidence.
takeaways.source_label: Call the Map (civicAPI, from state and county offices)

takeaways.headline: Michigan: about a third of active voters had already voted when polls opened
takeaways.detail: State data show 32.9% of Michigan's active registered voters had cast ballots by 7 AM ET Tuesday, including 750,469 early in-person votes; 2,313,165 ballots had been cast as of Monday morning. Michigan doesn't register by party, so this is turnout, not direction.
takeaways.source_label: CBS Detroit citing Michigan state data

takeaways.headline: North Carolina's final early vote: registered Democrats up 12.25 points
takeaways.detail: The state's own file shows 2,828,288 accepted ballots: 1,085,329 from registered Democrats, 738,750 Republicans and 995,435 unaffiliated, a 12.25-point Democratic edge versus about 7.0 at the same point in 2022 (tracker). Registration isn't vote choice.
takeaways.source_label: NC State Board of Elections absentee file

takeaways.headline: Iowa's final early vote still leans less Democratic than 2022
takeaways.detail: 498,713 early ballots, with registered Democrats ahead by 10.7 points versus 17.5 at the same point in 2022. Volume is up 35%.
takeaways.source_label: Call the Map (Iowa Secretary of State data)

takeaways.headline: Florida: Republicans' pre-Election Day ballot lead is smaller than in 2022
takeaways.detail: Registered Republicans led mail and early ballots by 133,177 (2,176,256 R vs 2,043,079 D of 5,408,792) per the Division of Elections on Nov 2, versus about 300,000 in 2022 per the Miami Herald. Election Day in-person voting, which leans Republican, is still under way. This is turnout by registration, not votes.
takeaways.source_label: FL Division of Elections via floridapredictions.com; Miami Herald

takeaways.headline: Trader odds: Democrats about 76-78% to win the Senate
takeaways.detail: Kalshi 76%, Polymarket 78% for Democratic Senate control as of 8:03 AM MT. Iowa is near a coin flip (52-53%). These are trader odds, not a forecast or a call.
takeaways.source_label: ArbTrader (Kalshi and Polymarket)

takeaways.headline: Overall: mixed, tilting slightly toward Democrats compared with 2022
takeaways.detail: North Carolina and Texas lean toward Democrats compared with 2022, Iowa leans toward Republicans, and Maine looks about the same. Kansas, Michigan, Ohio, Alaska and South Carolina have no like-for-like 2022 comparison. This is turnout, not votes.
takeaways.source_label: NC State Board of Elections; Texas SOS via early.professorbutts.com; Call the Map

takeaways.headline: Texas: early voting grew faster in Democratic-leaning counties than in Republican-leaning ones
takeaways.detail: In the 8 counties Democrats won by 20+ points, early votes are up 47.6% from 2022 (1.29 million vs 876,000). In the 221 counties Republicans won by 20+ points, they're up 34.0% (2.27 million vs 1.69 million). Statewide, 7.72 million voted early, up 40.5% from 2022 but down 14.8% from 2024. Texas has no party registration, so this compares places, not voters.
takeaways.source_label: Texas Secretary of State county early-vote data, compiled by early.professorbutts.com

takeaways.headline: North Carolina early ballots lean more Democratic than in 2022 (checked against the state's file)
takeaways.detail: The state's own file shows 2,819,922 accepted early ballots. Registered Democrats lead registered Republicans by 12.2 points, compared with a 6.9-point Democratic lead at the same point in 2022, per the Call the Map tracker. About 1 million ballots came from unaffiliated voters, who could go either way.
takeaways.source_label: North Carolina State Board of Elections absentee file

takeaways.headline: South Carolina's final early vote: 1,043,810 ballots
takeaways.detail: In-person early voting ended Oct 31 with 1,043,810 ballots, per the state election commission. South Carolina has no party registration, and no comparable 2022 county figures were available, so this doesn't show a direction.
takeaways.source_label: South Carolina Election Commission

takeaways.headline: Iowa early ballots lean less Democratic than in 2022
takeaways.detail: Among about 464,000 early ballots, registered Democrats lead by 12.3 points, down from an 18.7-point Democratic lead at the same point in 2022. Total early ballots are up 36% from 2022.
takeaways.source_label: Call the Map early-vote tracker

right.author: DataRepublican (@DataRepublican)

left.author: Kyle Griffin (@kylegriffin1)

if_trends_hold.note: Swing model not run yet: no county-level vote pull this hour. North Carolina and South Carolina counts are still mostly early votes.

gop_meter.headline: Worse than expected for Republicans so far
gop_meter.reason: Democrats flipped North Carolina (NBC News projection) and Republicans held Florida, but Moody leads only 50.8% to 48.1% at 96% in per AP versus a Moody +5.8 polling average and Trump +13.1 in 2024; South Carolina's Andrews (D) leads 52.6% to 45.7% at 49% in versus a Graham +2.2 average, with Republican-leaning Election Day votes still out.
gop_meter.basis: Model read vs polling averages, not a call
